obligation: HIPAA Security Rule: Hospital System
applies: Yes (covered entity; also business associate of 64 practices)
basis: A health care provider that sends claims and eligibility as standard electronic transactions is a covered entity (45 CFR 160.103). The Hospital System extends its EHR to 64 independent practices as their business associate. No size exemption; 164.306(b) affects how, not whether

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule: Health Plan
applies: Yes (covered entity; also business associate of 40 ASO plans)
basis: A health plan is a covered entity; the definition of health plan in 45 CFR 160.103 lists the Medicare Advantage program. The Hospital System and the Health Plan are separate subsidiaries with no affiliated covered entity designation (45 CFR 164.105(b)), so each is a separate covered entity

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule: College
basis: The College runs no health clinic and bills no health plan. Immunization and clearance records it holds are education records under FERPA, excluded from PHI (160.103, paragraph (2)(i)). Students on rotation are hospital workforce under the Hospital System's program

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule: corporate shared services
basis: Corporate shared services in the parent creates, receives, maintains and transmits both covered entities' ePHI on SYS-G1 to SYS-G3 under intercompany BAAs

obligation: HIPAA Privacy Rule: Hospital System
basis: Covered entity. PHI sent to the Health Plan is a disclosure between separate covered entities: the routine ADT feed relies on 164.506(c)(4) and needs a standard minimum-necessary protocol (164.514(d)(3)(i))

obligation: HIPAA Privacy Rule: Health Plan
basis: Covered entity. Routine requests for hospital data need a standard protocol (164.514(d)(4)(ii)); minimum necessary (164.502(b))

obligation: HIPAA Privacy Rule: corporate shared services
basis: Uses and disclosures limited to the intercompany BAAs

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule: Hospital System
basis: Own notices to individuals, HHS and media as a covered entity; notices to the 64 community-connect practices as their business associate

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule: Health Plan
basis: Own notices as a separate covered entity; notices to the 40 ASO plans as their business associate under BAA terms that vary by employer

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule: corporate shared services
basis: Notice to both covered entities as their business associate

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule: College
basis: Not a covered entity or business associate

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule NPRM (2025): all divisions and group
basis: Not a final rule; tracked for planning for the two health divisions and corporate

obligation: FDA premarket cybersecurity (cyber devices): Hospital System
applies: No direct duty (manufacturers); used as a procurement lever
basis: Section 524B binds device manufacturers. The Hospital System buys about 52,000 networked devices and uses SBOM and patch support terms at purchase. Not applicable to the Health Plan or the College

obligation: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule: all divisions and group
basis: 16 CFR 318.1 excludes HIPAA covered entities and business associates acting as such; the College operates no personal health record

obligation: 42 CFR Part 2 (SUD records): all divisions and group
basis: No hospital holds itself out as providing substance use disorder diagnosis, treatment or referral as a specialized program; Part 2 records received from outside programs are flagged in the EHR and handled by the Privacy Officer case by case. No other division runs a Part 2 program

obligation: CMS emergency preparedness condition of participation: Hospital System
applies: Yes (all 9 hospitals, unified and integrated program)
basis: Every hospital participates in Medicare and Medicaid and elected the unified program under 482.15(f). 482.15(g) does not apply: no transplant program
analyzed_in: P03 (gap-analysis.csv, G-070 to G-096); P05; P08

obligation: CMS emergency preparedness: Health Plan, College and group
basis: None of these is a certified provider type

obligation: HPH Cybersecurity Performance Goals: all divisions and group
applies: Voluntary (Hospital System and Health Plan; not applicable to the College)
basis: Used as a maturity overlay

obligation: HHS 405(d) HICP: all divisions and group
applies: Voluntary (HICP volume for large organizations; not applicable to the College)
basis: Used as a maturity overlay

obligation: HITECH recognized security practices: Hospital System, Health Plan and corporate
applies: Yes (mitigating factor; not applicable to the College)
basis: HHS considers recognized practices in place for the prior 12 months when it sets fines and remedies for covered entities and business associates

obligation: CIRCIA (proposed): Hospital System and College
basis: Not in effect. If finalized as proposed it would cover all 9 hospitals (100 or more beds) and the College as a Title IV participant (N61-R06)

obligation: Section 1557 patient care decision support tools: Hospital System
basis: The Hospital System receives federal financial assistance through Medicare and Medicaid; the sepsis model, the deterioration index and the CT triage tool are in use

obligation: Section 1557 patient care decision support tools: Health Plan
applies: Under counsel review before the AI triage pilot reaches production
basis: Medicare Advantage payments are federal financial assistance; whether a UM triage tool supports clinical decision-making is under counsel review

obligation: Section 1557 patient care decision support tools: College
basis: The College provides no patient care

obligation: EMTALA: Hospital System
basis: 9 Medicare-participating hospitals with emergency departments; governs screening and diversion when the EHR is down

obligation: Medicare Advantage (42 CFR 422.101, 422.118, 422.137, 422.566): Health Plan
basis: The Health Plan holds a Medicare Advantage contract and runs a UM program; the AI triage pilot is in shadow mode. Not applicable to the other divisions

obligation: GLBA privacy and safeguards: Health Plan
basis: An insurer holding member nonpublic personal information; state insurance authorities enforce GLBA for insurers (15 U.S.C. 6805(a)(6))

obligation: NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law #668: Health Plan
citation: NAIC Model #668 as enacted by each state
basis: The Health Plan is a licensee in 5 states; duties apply where a state enacted the model, and text varies by state

obligation: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation: all divisions
basis: No division holds a New York insurance license

obligation: GLBA Safeguards Rule (Title IV institutions): College
applies: Yes (agreed in the Program Participation Agreement)
basis: A Title IV participant holding customer information on about 9,600 students and 31,000 former students; the 314.6 exception (fewer than 5,000 consumers) does not apply

obligation: GLBA Safeguards Rule: corporate as College service provider and affiliate
basis: Corporate hosts the College's administrative file shares and supports it through the group SOC; the College must oversee it as a service provider

obligation: FERPA: College
basis: The College receives funds under Department of Education programs (Title IV). Disclosures to clinical sites rest on signed consent (99.30); corporate and SaaS vendors are school officials

obligation: FERPA: Hospital System, Health Plan and group
applies: No (hospitals receive placement data with consent; corporate is bound as a school official through the College)
basis: Only the College is an educational agency or institution

obligation: Federal Student Aid breach reporting: College
basis: A Title IV participant must report an actual or suspected breach to FSA immediately

obligation: COPPA Rule: College
basis: Adult students; no child-directed services

obligation: CIPA (E-Rate): College
basis: Not a K-12 school or library receiving E-Rate discounts

obligation: HIPAA hybrid entity rules: College
basis: No covered health care component

obligation: SEC cybersecurity disclosure: group
basis: The holding company is an SEC registrant; divisions contribute incident facts through the group

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (breach notification): all divisions
basis: The group holds personal information of Florida residents (6 hospitals, the Health Plan and College students in Florida); other states' breach laws apply where affected individuals reside (Florida is the worked example)

obligation: Intercompany BAAs and College services agreement: corporate with each division
basis: Hospital System BAA (2021) does not mention community-connect practices' PHI; Health Plan BAA (2022) covers the ASO plans' PHI; College agreement (2025) sets same-day phone notice and omits the 99.33(a) redisclosure limits

obligation: Community-connect agreements and BAAs: Hospital System
basis: Incident and breach notice to each of the 64 practices; the practices asked for a SOC 2 Type 2 report by the end of 2027

obligation: ASO employer plan BAAs and SOC 1 commitments: Health Plan
basis: 40 ASO BAAs with notice terms that vary by employer; SOC 1 Type 2 report on ASO claims administration

obligation: SOC 2 scoping by division
citation: AICPA Trust Services Criteria; customer contracts
applies: Planned for the community-connect service; Health Plan relies on SOC 1; College out of scope
basis: Only the community-connect service has user entities asking for SOC 2
